verdict.rationale: Missive's own rules engine runs automations in the background without user action. Rules can run multi-step sequences over time, with delays in calendar or business hours, and act on conversations (e.g., label, notify, reassign). Rules can also create drafts, and AI rules are mentioned. missing for 10: detailed documentation of AI-driven rules and their triggers/actions, evidence of a first-party autonomous AI agent acting on new mail (the triage example relies on external MCP agents), independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Rules can now run in steps over time. Each step waits, checks its own conditions, then acts on the same conversation.
Escalate unanswered support emails: label at 24 hrs, notify the lead at 48, reassign at 72.
Delays can count calendar time or business hours.
Drafts created outside the composer, by the assistant, by a rule, or through the API and MCP server
Your AI rules, saved models, and assistant conversations stay intact
